findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the eval YAML for `code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries` uses `name: code_review_emits_valid_findings` (not `emits_valid_findings`) as its deterministic gating scorer, matching the `outputs: code_review_findings` contract.
evidence: `eval_scorers.py:403-408`: `'emits_valid_findings': _schema_review_result` (plan-review schema) vs `'code_review_emits_valid_findings': _schema_code_review_findings`
Plan specifies `outputs: code_review_findings` for the prompt — implying the code-review output schema applies

The portability eval (`.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml:19`) uses `emits_valid_findings` and is a plan-review criterion — pattern should NOT be copied verbatim for a code-review criterion
findings.finding: The eval YAML for this code-review criterion must use the scorer name `code_review_emits_valid_findings`, not `emits_valid_findings`. In `eval_scorers.py`, `emits_valid_findings` maps to `_schema_review_result` (the plan-review schema), while `code_review_emits_valid_findings` maps to `_schema_code_review_findings` — the schema for `outputs: code_review_findings`. Using the wrong scorer would validate the output against the plan-review schema, silently producing incorrect calibration verdicts for a code-review finder.
scenarios: Eval YAML authored with `name: emits_valid_findings` validates against plan-review schema; a code-review `{findings: [...]}` payload may pass or fail for wrong reasons
Strict scorer-name validation (`validate_eval_spec(..., strict=True)`) would pass because `emits_valid_findings` IS registered — the bug is semantic, not structural
findings.suggested_fix: In the eval spec under `scorers`, use `name: code_review_emits_valid_findings` so the deterministic gate validates against the code-review findings schema (`_schema_code_review_findings`).

findings.location: Eval Contract section; AC3 verify command; `.rebar/evals/code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries.eval.yaml` (to be authored)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace hardcoded `.venv/bin/python` / `.venv/bin/rebar` in all AC verification commands with a platform-neutral invocation (e.g. `python` / `rebar` resolved from the active virtualenv, or a `make verify-criterion` target that abstracts the path) so the ACs are runnable on Windows developer workstations.
evidence: `.venv/bin/python -c 'import json; d=json.load(...)'` — AC block 1
`.venv/bin/python -c 'from pathlib import Path; ...' && .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_review_phase_boundaries.py'` — AC block 2
`.venv/bin/rebar criteria eval project.review-phase-boundaries --runs 3 --output json | .venv/bin/python -c ...'` — AC block 3
Windows virtualenv layout places scripts at `.venv\Scripts\`, not `.venv/bin/`; POSIX `&&` chaining works in PS7 but the paths themselves resolve to nothing on Windows.
Supported matrix cell: Platform and venue — Windows developer workstations.
findings.finding: All six AC verification commands use the POSIX virtualenv path `.venv/bin/python` and `.venv/bin/rebar`, chained with POSIX `&&`. On Windows, Python virtualenvs place executables at `.venv\Scripts\python.exe` and `.venv\Scripts\rebar.exe`; the `/bin/` subdirectory does not exist.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — all six AC verification command blocks (e.g. `.venv/bin/python -c 'import json; ...'`, `.venv/bin/rebar criteria eval ...`, `.venv/bin/pytest ...`)
scenarios: A developer running the AC verification commands on a Windows workstation (supported matrix cell: Windows platform) receives `The system cannot find the path specified` or equivalent for every `.venv/bin/python` invocation, making all six ACs unverifiable on that platform.
